STEP 1 - Scene: This looks like cooked strips of cured meat, most likely bacon-style or turkey/pork bacon-style slices, arranged loosely on a plate. No other food is visible.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 26 cm across (dinner-plate size). Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 531 cm^2 (for the round equivalent; the square plate is similar in usable area).

STEP 3 - Items: Seven or so strips of cooked, reddish-brown meat strips with crisp edges. No visible oil or sauce pooling beyond light surface sheen.

STEP 4 - Area: The strips together cover roughly 30% of the plate. Taking the largest strips and the overlapping cluster, the coverage is about 30% (≈160 cm^2).

STEP 5 - Volume: Strips are thin, about 0.4 cm thick on average as a pile. 160 cm^2 x 0.4 cm ≈ 64 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cooked cured meat strips, bulk density ~0.9 g/ml. 64 ml x 0.9 ≈ 58 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked bacon-style meat is about 450 kcal per 100 g (fatty, cured pork bacon-type). 58 g x 4.5 ≈ 260 kcal. (If it is a leaner turkey or meat-based product, the value would be lower, ~250 kcal/100 g, giving about 145 kcal; I use the bacon-style figure as the more likely reading of these crisp strips.)

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Seven thin strips covering about a third of a dinner plate at roughly 55–60 g is plausible for a few rashers of bacon-style meat.
